title: What's new in the Gemma open model family

segments.text: [MUSIC PLAYING]
OLIVIER LACOMBE: Hey, everyone.
Welcome to What's New in the Gemma Open Model Family.
My name is Olivier.
I'm the product lead for Gemma.
And today, I will be joined by Gus, a product
manager on our team, and Ian Ballantyne, our developer
relation engineer.
So what is Gemma?
Gemma is an open weight large language
model at Google DeepMind.
We started Gemma in 2024 with a simple premise.
How do we create a model that you can run everywhere and fully
customize to your needs?
That created two requirements for us.
Number 1, make sure that the model is reasonably sized.
Number 2, make an open weight model that you can
fine tune to your wheel.
With Gemma 3, we did exactly that.
We created a multi-model family of model running
from IoT devices at 1 billion parameter
to larger consumer GPU at 27 billion parameter.
And we made sure to apply one thing which
is part of our philosophy, a.k.a., give you
the highest efficiency possible running on your local machine.
And a couple of weeks ago, we announced
Gemma 4, our most capable open model to date.
Thank you.
[APPLAUSE]
We apply the same philosophy with Gemma 4,
giving you four model size ranging
from 2 billion parameters to 31 billion parameters
that you can run everywhere.
You want to run at the edge on IoT devices?
Use our 2 billion parameter model.
You want to run on a higher-end phone or lower-end laptop?
Use a 4 billion parameter model.
You have a more powerful machine and you want the highest
efficiency and latency?
Use a mixture of expert at 26 billion parameter.
Finally, you're looking to fine tune
and have the highest quality possible?
We have a 31 B ready to go.
And we maintain our philosophy around efficiency.
Our Gemma model, here evaluated on LLM Arena,
are scoring as well as model 20x the size.
We want to make sure that you have the best
bang for the buck, the highest amount of intelligence per watt.
Our models are highly efficient by training.
As you can see on the right-hand side,
we've improved Gemma 4 capabilities
across the whole spectrum, from text use case, creative writing,
code, or reasoning with science, legal, and so many other areas.
The reception so far has been fantastic,
and we cannot thank you more.
We have more than 100 million downloads.
We had more than 6 million downloads of the AI Edge
gallery, which you can demo outside,
and the reception has been, again, incredible.
We are very, very happy to see that people
are using and enjoying the Gemma 4 models.
In terms of capabilities, we've changed a couple of things
compared to Gemma 3.
Now, our models have a larger context window.
We move from 32,000 tokens to 128,000 for small size,
up to 256,000 for 31B and 26B.
Now, all of our models come with both reasoning, a.k.a. thinking,
and function calling, making them fully
ready for the agentic era.
Finally, we changed our license.
We moved away from a custom Gemma license
to a popular Apache 2.0 license, giving you full control
when you deploy in production.
[APPLAUSE]
We know that the Apache 2.0 license was very well received,
and we are very happy.
We want to see Gemma being used more in your pipeline.
In terms of capabilities, I want to highlight a couple of things.
On the vision side, because we know
our models are being used at the edge,
we made sure to give you the highest amount of efficiency.
We have now variable aspect ratio images
and visual understanding.
We can process charts, document, and screenshot better than ever,
and we have multimodal translation
being built from the ground up.
On the agentic side, our models are
fully ready with multi-step planning, tool use,
and autonomous task completion.
You can now use them in whatever agentic pipeline
you have ready to go.
Finally, audio understanding on the smallest size
has been completely redone from the ground up.
We are more than ever multilingual in essence
with speech understanding and have good transcription
and translation capabilities.
Of course, text understanding, we have that since Gemma 1.
We continue to be state of the art in English
when it comes to our main Gemma family,
and we've expanded that across internationalization, which
is something we'll cover after.
From a vision standpoint, a couple of things to highlight.
We have object detection.
We can do bounding boxes, which is quite important if you
want to use Gemma in IoT use cases or robotics use cases.
And again, as I mentioned, we have multi-modal translation
from image input, and we'll show you
more demos like in the rest of the presentation.
Gemma comes with multiple architecture
ready to go for where you want to deploy them.
If you want to push Gemma at the edge,
we have per-layer embedding, which
is a new technique we've developed for Gemma 4
to optimize efficiency.
If you want to deploy them on your laptop,
we have two types of architecture-- a 31B Dense,
which is going to make fine tuning easier and help us get
the highest amount of intelligence per tokens--
per parameter, sorry-- and the other one is a 26B MoE,
giving you the highest efficiency in terms of runtime.
From a benchmark standpoint, I don't want
to spend too much time there.
Please go and try the Gemma model
and see if they fit your use case.
What I want to point your attention to is the capability
of Gemma 4 E2B model compared to the previous generation at 27B.
Our 2B model this cycle is matching or even better than
our 27B last year, and that makes me very excited about
the future.
I'd love to see if next year we're able to give you the 31B
capabilities in your pocket, running on your phone fully
locally.
I think that makes up for a very exciting future.
Now, I've talked about multilinguality,
and I wanted to show you that it means a lot to us.
On the left-hand side, you can see
EuroEval, which is an independent benchmark
leaderboard where the model is being rated
across European languages.
And what you can see there is that all of our Gemma models
are scoring pretty well.
Our 31B specifically ranked from between number 1 to number 5
on almost all European languages,
and that is across open source and closed source model.
On the right-hand side, you have another example
where we're comparing Gemma to other very successful models
on Japanese languages, and our Gemma model
is getting very close to GPT 5.4.
We have very strong compatibility
with Southeast Asian language.
And Korean is another language where we excel at.
Now, another benchmark which was quite amusing--
FoodTruck Bench.
So I didn't know this one before releasing Gemma 4.
It's actually measuring the reasoning capabilities
of the model as well as the function calling.
And we found out that the 31B is, to quote the line,
a beast at that.
The model is doing extremely well
in an environment where you need to have deep reasoning
and, I would say, reasonable function calling.
As you can see here, Gemma 31B is competing with DeepSeek v4
Pro, which is a more than 1 trillion parameter model
and lots of top-line closed-source model.
In terms of efficiency, as I mentioned to you
at the beginning of our presentation,
we want to make sure we give you the best bang for the bucks.
LLM Arena has done a couple of analyses on that front.
We've also released MTP Drafter, enabling speculative decoding
on a model lineup, giving you up to 3x speedup when it comes
to your decode speed.
So if you haven't used it yet, I would massively
recommend you to move towards MTP
and gain the highest efficiency performance on your Gemma
implementation.
Now, again, Gemma being fully open weight and compatible
with the open source ecosystem, we
have support across the board.
We are supported from a mobile and web app standpoint.
You also have all your favorite softwares
ready to go with Gemma 4 on your local machine,
and we have deep implementation on the Cloud server.
And this year specifically, we also
made sure that we had a day 0 implementation with Gemma 4
in the Android ecosystem.
So you can either try our smallest Gemma running directly
on your phone, available through the API that Android is exposing
to developers, or to code your Android apps locally with
a Gemma 26B model when you're on the plane or you don't have
access to the Gemma API.
And now, I will pass over to Gus,
who will cover our implementation in the Cloud.
[APPLAUSE]
GUS MARTINS: Hi, everyone.
Good morning.

Very happy to be here.
Nice to see some familiar faces.
As Olivier was saying, Gemma is pretty cool.

The endpoint is yours.

This is on Gemini Enterprise Agent platform,

So for example, if you want to do some post

Cloud platform.

and you do a further fine tuning and customizing the model.

When we talk in deploying using Cloud,
there are multiple levels of difficulty or challenges
that you face, and that depends on how much you understand
and how much you want to use time to manage your servers,
your endpoints.
Gemini Enterprise Agent platform, I would say,
is in the middle.
You have some control, but you also-- there's
a lot of stuff that helps you do it easier.
When we talk about Google Cloud Kubernetes Engine,
I would say this is more advanced,
but you also have control of everything.
You have access to every knob.
You can change any configuration that you want.
We also have, of course, Gemma there.
We have recipes for you to easily follow and deploy.
But there, you have access to the VM,
and you can change anything you want.
Of course, we have recipes with everything preconfigured for you
with the best parameters.
But if you want to change something
to optimize for your infrastructure,
for your use case, you can go and do all of that.
You have total control and flexibility on these endpoints.
Of course, everything is always optimized for performance.
We work with them to also have the MTP models already
available for you whenever you want to use,
and this enables you to create all your agent works already
with the servers there.
So you have all of that.
So when you talk about GKE, you have access
to create this provision.
You have access to all these GPUs.
You can use TPUs also.
You can use any kind of hardware you want.
You choose how you create your VM,
and you can deploy that and start serving.
It's pretty quick, but it needs you more expertise, I would say.
GKE gives you all the power, but you also
have to pay attention to all the details.
But if you want something that's the easiest solution,
we have Cloud Run.
So you can also very easily two lines of code
deploy Gemma using Cloud Run.
What's the difference from the other two?
Cloud Run gives you an endpoint.
You just deploy and it gives you an endpoint.
This endpoint you can access, do queries, and use Gemma
the same way you would use local or other providers.
But if you don't use, the server will spin down and scale to 0.
Or if your app becomes very popular, you get many requests,
it can also scale up to maybe 100 GPUs,
and it can do all of that.
And when you start from 0-- for example,
let's suppose your server goes down because nobody
was using for whatever reason.
When you go back up, it takes you
a couple of seconds of warm-up, and the endpoint
is already there.
So it's super optimized for you if you
want to do something quicker, and this is the easiest
solution, I would say.
So we have Cloud Run as the easiest,
most straightforward solution.
We have Gemini Enterprise, which was called Vertex.
Gemini Enterprise, that's the middle term.
You have some more options and something that will help you.
And then you have GKE, which you have access and control
of everything.
So you choose wherever you want to play the game there.
That's great.
Now you understand what Gemma is.
We showed you all the capabilities, what it can do,
where, and how you can deploy.
That's great, but let's go a little bit
beyond Gus, Olivier, Ian just saying how amazing it is.
Let's try to show some cool demos and show it working real--
doing some fun stuff.
We have a bunch of demos, and we are going to go from--
let's start from this side.
We're going to go from Enterprise, or the 31B model,
which is the stronger one, show you some more advanced use
cases.
Then we're going to show something

Then, we'll show something that runs
on your phone that could be already running on your phone.
We have demos outside also, and then we'll
show some IoT and robotics.
Let's go over all of this.
I hope you get excited with this.
The first one-- I like this very much.
Let me see if I can do play.
So what's happening here?
I want you to pay attention to the query that happened there.
The idea is, do you know those bikes

system?
What happened here is we asked Gemma, hey, help
me optimize the revenue.
And here is the database.
So the setup, now that it's running, now
I can explain everything else.
The setup is we get the ADK framework,
the Agent Development Kit, running using Gemma 31B
that's on Cloud Run.
We configure it to have a BigQuery MCP server connected.
So the model can do queries to this database
that it doesn't know.
It's just a database.
This database is, of course, the Citi Bikes database.
It has all the points where the bikes are, their demand.
There's time when bikes were used, all of that--
all the analytical database you would expect.
With that, we asked the model, hey,
help me optimize for revenue.
And all that you are seeing here, this is not accelerated.
This is real speed.
The model creates a plan to, first of all,
understand what's available on this database.
Like you would do if I ask you this thing,
first thing you would do is let me take a look on the database
and what's available.
That's exactly what the model does.
Oh, let me see what is available in this database.
From there, it devises a plan to find
where it can optimize the service to get more bikes,
to add other points with bikes.
It tries to do a bunch of experiments
until we get to the end and show these
are the places where you have to increase the number of bicycles.
And in doing that, you can see there,
for example, there is a moment it
makes a mistake when it tries to join two tables,
and there is a type that's wrong.
It can fix this.
Oh, there's an error.
Let me fix this join--
all of this by itself.
There is no other user turn.
There was one query at the beginning,
and this runs for three minutes, the model trying stuff.
It does, and then it makes a mistake.
It regenerates.
It fix something.
Oh, I found something new.
And it keeps going, keeps going, trying to optimize the service.
And this is a pretty good example.
I strongly recommend you try stuff similar.
The model, it shows that Gemma, 31B specifically,
is very strong on planning and executing that plan,
even if it has to execute code somewhere,
run a query somewhere, or get more information from other
sources, think more, join this information,
and keep on this planning.
This is the power of Gemma 31B.
I guess this is the-- so it's found the best locations,
and it knows that's the answer.
So it's showing, What are the 10 best locations
to improve the service? right there, based on all these
back and forth.
So now I know.
Thank you.
[APPLAUSE]
Gemma's pretty cool.
Nice.
This is one.
Running on server, you can do that, connect to MCP.
Let's go into another one.
This is using Firebase AI Logic.
And the challenge here is a little bit different.
Imagine you are running the model on your phone.
If you try to run models on your phone,
there are some moments where the model might not
be available for you on your phone
because the phone is maybe old, doesn't have enough memory,
or something like that.
So if you're an app developer and you
build a feature that requires the model
to be there, when the model is not there,
you face a challenge automatically there.
What do you do?
One option is to have a hybrid solution where
you have the model running on the phone when possible.
And when it's not possible, you call the model
on the cloud provider.
So you have a hybrid solution that uses both local-- oh,
it stop-- you saw the video.
It runs local or on the server depending
on what you want to do.
Firebase AI Logic helps you do that.
You configure for it to prioritize local.
And if it's not available local, it
will just route the same query to your server
that you configure there.
So that gives you an easier way to do a hybrid solution.
Why this matters?
Because it simplifies your life as a developer.
Because if you have to do that by hand,
it can be quite annoying and hard.
So Firebase AI Logic helps you do all of that.
It can use your AICore implementation locally
if it's available on a Pixel, on a Samsung device.
If it's not available, you can call the server
and make this, from the user perspective,
completely transparent.
You don't know that you're missing anything,
and you implement the same logic.
This is also already available.
For the next demo, I'd like to call Ian.
He'll show you a bunch of more demos, and I'll come back later.
Thank you.
[APPLAUSE]
IAN BALLANTYNE: Yes, thank you very much, Gus.
So my name is Ian.
I'm the developer experience lead for Gemma.
And the next thing I want to talk to you
about is Gemma's coding capabilities.
So all of our models can code even down to the E2B model.
And what we're going to show you here
is a demonstration of a game called
AIventure, where you can vibe code along using the model.
And we'll play the video so you can have a look.
[VIDEO PLAYBACK]
- Want to learn how to build agentic workflows
and integrate vibe coding into your apps?
Well, we built AIventure, an open source retro dungeon
crawler that doubles as a gen AI masterclass for developers.

AIventure is powered by Google's Gemma 4 open weights model.
First, we'll explore vibe coding.

on the fly and renders it locally in an iframe
to validate the constraints.
Next, you'll build agentic behaviors.

you must prompt a robot NPC.

executes specific tool calls to locate a hidden switch,
and interacts with the Phaser JS game engine to solve the puzzle.
The biggest takeaway?
You have complete flexibility in how the model is served.
You can run Gemma 4 entirely locally,
with zero ongoing server costs, using Transformers.js
in the browser, or by plugging into Ollama or LLM
Studio via their OpenAI compatible interfaces.
Need cloud scale?
A simple config change routes your request
to the right Gemini API or Google Cloud.
Ready to look under the hood?
Scan the QR code, and explore the GitHub repo,

Take on the quest to expand your AI tooling

IAN BALLANTYNE: Thank you.
